content: Breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication due to potential risks to the infant. This restriction should also be followed for at least three months after the final dose. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. It is essential to maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if someone experiences severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. It is crucial to attend all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, it is important to receive the medication as scheduled. This medication is administered by a healthcare professional through an intravenous injection over two hours. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. Before receiving this medication, your doctor may prescribe other medications, such as acetaminophen, diphenhydramine, corticosteroids, antibiotics, or antiviral drugs, to prevent side effects and infections. Common side effects may include diarrhea, stomach or abdominal pain, fatigue, headache, tremors, difficulty sleeping, or mouth sores. However, this medication may also cause serious side effects. Your doctor has prescribed this drug because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks. This medication may increase the risk of a rare but potentially fatal brain infection called progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML). Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. Before receiving this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This drug may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Inform your healthcare provider that you are using this medication before receiving any immunizations or vaccinations. This medication may increase the risk of a serious infection caused by the bacteria Listeria. During treatment and for some time afterward, avoid foods that may contain Listeria, such as deli meats, unpasteurized milk and cheese products, soft cheeses, and undercooked meat, seafood, or poultry. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your doctor. You should not become pregnant while using this medication, as it may harm an unborn baby. Your doctor will likely order a pregnancy test before starting this medication. Discuss reliable forms of birth control to use during treatment and for at least three months after the last dose. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk, so breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment and for at least three months after the final dose. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all products you use and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If you experience side effects, contact your doctor for medical advice. In the U.S., you can report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088. In Canada, you can report side effects to Health Canada. This information is a summary and does not contain all details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
